lines:
Responsibilities: Is the host's sole core-facing execution port. It admits and dispatches only a durable core-issued ApprovedInvocationEnvelopeV1 and accepts generation-fenced HostControlEnvelopeV1 cancellation/timeout controls; it validates protocol/schema, invocation/decision identity, pinned binding hash, enforced scopes, budget, deadline, cancellation token, lease handles, and maximum payload sizes before any adapter observes work.
Owned runtime state: ephemeral InvocationAdmissionV1 records keyed by invocationId, same-ID acceptance/dedup facts, dispatch milestone, bounded per-invocation stream window, cancellation registration, and host-generation correlation. None is canonical and all may be rebuilt only from reconciled core controls.
Versioned ports and contracts: ApprovedInvocationPortV1 receives ApprovedInvocationEnvelopeV1; HostEventPortV1 returns HostInvocationEventV1 containing Accepted, FlowControl, Progress, ApprovalRequest, Usage, Artifact, TerminalOutcome, or RejectedDefiniteNotStarted. It resolves only exact CapabilityDescriptorV1 records and never substitutes a binding.
Failure and degraded behavior: malformed, stale-generation, expired, oversized, unknown, or hash-mismatched envelopes fail closed before dispatch. Disconnect or backpressure stops new admissions while reserving control capacity; after a possible start it reports facts to outcome normalization and never guesses that an effect did not occur.
Security and authority: it cannot create or broaden authority, grant approval, select a graph destination, mint a lease, access a secret value, or accept a worker connection. The worker has no host channel.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: bounded queues, explicit flow-control credits, monotonic deadlines, latency/queue/validation metrics, secret-free correlation logs, and identical length-delimited Aworkit framing on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Non-responsibilities: no workflow routing/retry policy, provider/tool implementation, process supervision policy, canonical event commit, history persistence, or side-effect replay.

data.name: Approved Invocation Gateway & Runtime
data.technology: Rust async local-RPC gateway and bounded invocation runtime
